- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained upward trends, particularly when true values rise sharply (e.g., 81+ range).
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects with a lag — adjust downward by 1–2% of forecast value after peak.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate price pullback after strong rallies.
- Forecast horizon 1–3 days shows higher error; model is overly optimistic in short-term moves.
- Model exhibits “sticky” bias — if true price is above 80, forecast often stays above 80 without adjusting for volatility.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model overweights recent highs and fails to account for supply/demand shocks.
- Corrective rule: if true price exceeds forecast by >3%, reduce next forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
